reason: The cited lines show JavaScript being eval'd inside Playwright page/locator.evaluate and returning the result, so this is browser-page execution rather than arbitrary host execution. Because arbitrary evaluated page JavaScript can initiate browser requests to URLs chosen in the supplied expression, the lines support SINK. They do not by themselves establish that the returned value is non-public secret data, nor that it is attacker-controllable content; that depends on the page/context and expression source, which are not settled by these lines.
